title: Cities of Refuge
lead: Six towns where someone who had killed by accident could flee from the family avenger until his case was heard (Exodus 21:13; Numbers 35; Deuteronomy 19; Joshua 20). Early Christians read them as a picture of refuge in Christ.

sections.b: Exodus 21:13 promises "a place" for the one who killed without intent, while the deliberate murderer may be taken even from the altar (Exodus 21:14; 1 Kings 2:28–34). Numbers 35 names six cities, three on each side of the Jordan, where the killer stays until the high priest dies; Deuteronomy 19:1–13 tells Israel to keep the roads to them open. Joshua 20 lists them: Kedesh, Shechem and Hebron west of the Jordan, Bezer, Ramoth and Golan to the east. Hebrews 6:18 uses the same picture for believers who run for safety to the hope set before them.
